name: Hidden Passage Trail
company: Tennessee State Parks, Pickett CCC Memorial State Park
unique: A five and a half mile loop along the rim of the Pickett State Forest gorge, past sandstone bluffs, rock shelters big enough to camp under, a natural bridge and overlooks into a valley with no road in it.
buzz: Hikers call it the best loop in the state for its length, and the cliff edge campsites are the reason people carry a pack. The exposure is real and the trail is not for young children.

name: Currituck Beach Lighthouse
unique: A hundred and sixty two foot brick tower first lit in December 1875, the only Outer Banks lighthouse left unpainted so the brick shows, with two hundred and fourteen steps to a gallery above the Currituck Sound and the Atlantic.
buzz: The unpainted brick is what people notice first and the climb is the reason to stop. It is the least crowded of the Outer Banks lights because it is an hour north of the others.

name: Whalehead
unique: A 1920s Art Nouveau hunting lodge of twenty one thousand square feet built by a Philadelphia industrialist, with Tiffany style fixtures, a grand staircase and a basement billiard room, standing alone on the sound side of the northern Outer Banks.
buzz: The house is more ornate than the beach around it and that is the surprise. Tours cover the family, the servants and the waterfowl hunting that the house was built for.

name: Corolla Wild Horses
dates: Year round, tours daily weather permitting
company: Corolla Wild Horse Fund and licensed tour operators
unique: A herd of colonial Spanish mustangs living free on the northern beaches and sound side dunes, descendants of horses brought by explorers, now managed by a fund that asks visitors to stay fifty feet back and never feed them.
buzz: Tours run in open trucks over the sand and the horses are often right on the beach. The fund is explicit that the horses are wild and that the rules exist because people kept getting kicked.

name: Historic Corolla Village
company: Currituck County and the Corolla Wild Horse Fund
unique: A cluster of nineteenth and early twentieth century buildings under the live oaks behind the dunes, with a one room schoolhouse, a weather bureau station, a chapel and a boardwalk through the maritime forest.
buzz: It is the old Outer Banks before the beach houses, shaded and quiet, and the boardwalk is a good place to look for the horses without a truck tour.

name: Dismal Swamp State Park
unique: Fourteen thousand acres of Great Dismal Swamp on the North Carolina side of the line, with a network of straight logging roads now used as bike and hiking trails, a boardwalk over the canal and black bear, bobcat and barred owl in the woods.
buzz: The trails are flat, wide and empty, which makes it the best family bike ride in the northeast. Paddlers put in on the canal and the swamp forest closes in within a mile.

name: Dismal Swamp Canal Welcome Center
unique: A welcome center on the oldest continuously operating man made canal in the United States, dug by enslaved labor from 1793, where pleasure boats on the Intracoastal Waterway tie up at the dock and the exhibits explain the ditch that changed the map.
buzz: Boaters stop for the free dock and the shade, and the exhibits are better than a highway rest stop deserves. People are surprised the canal is still working.

name: Camden Heritage Museum and Historic Jail
unique: A county museum and the old jail beside the 1840s courthouse, with the records, tools, quilts and photographs of a county that has been farming the same flat land between the swamp and the sound since the 1770s.
buzz: Volunteers run it and the jail is the part children remember. It is small, free and the only place to understand Camden County indoors.

name: Museum of the Albemarle
customer: Families, school groups, regional history travellers
unique: A regional museum on the Pasquotank waterfront covering the Albemarle from the Algonquian towns through the watermen, with the official state historic boat, a shad boat built in the 1880s, and exhibits on the swamp, the canal and the Civil War.
buzz: It is free, air conditioned and the best introduction to northeastern North Carolina. The shad boat and the watermen exhibits are the ones people mention.

name: Elizabeth City Waterfront
cost: Free, slip free for visiting boats
unique: A downtown waterfront on the Pasquotank River with free docks for visiting boats, a tradition of welcoming cruisers with roses and wine, and a river walk that connects the historic district to the museum and the parks.
buzz: Cruisers on the Intracoastal plan stops here because the town meets them at the dock. Locals walk the river at sunset and the waterfront is the reason downtown has come back.

name: Elizabeth City Historic District
unique: Blocks of Victorian and early twentieth century commercial buildings and houses behind the waterfront, with a 1900s courthouse, churches with steeples and a Main Street that still has a department store and a hardware store.
buzz: The historic district is bigger than people expect for a town this size and it is walkable in an hour. The waterfront and the museum are both inside it.

name: Newbold-White House
customer: History travellers, architecture fans, school groups
unique: A 1730 brick house on the Perquimans River, the oldest brick dwelling in North Carolina, built by a Quaker family, with original woodwork, a detached kitchen and grounds that include the site of a seventeenth century Yeopim town.
buzz: The brick and the setting on the river are what people photograph. The association is honest that the land was the Yeopim's first, and the tour covers both.

name: Hertford Historic District
unique: A river town with the second oldest courthouse in North Carolina, a waterfront on the Perquimans, and blocks of eighteenth and nineteenth century houses including the 1730 Newbold-White House at the edge of town.
buzz: Small enough to walk in an hour and old enough to feel it. The waterfront dock is where people eat lunch and watch the river.

name: Perquimans River Waterfront
company: Town of Hertford and the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission
unique: A wide tidal river running into the Albemarle Sound, with a public ramp and dock at Hertford, cypress along the banks and enough backwater to lose an afternoon in.
buzz: Anglers fish the river for bass and catfish and paddlers work the creeks. Birders come for the herons and the occasional eagle, and it is quiet on weekdays.

name: Historic Murfreesboro
unique: A river town that was a center of education and culture in the early 1800s, with a walkable district of Federal and Greek Revival houses, a museum and several historic houses open by appointment through the historical association.
buzz: The association runs the tours and the town has kept more of its early fabric than most. People come for one house and end up walking the whole grid.

name: Chowan River
unique: A wide, slow river running from the Virginia line to the Albemarle, with cypress and tupelo along the banks, boat ramps at several landings and a bass and catfish fishery that locals keep quiet about.
buzz: Anglers say the river is underfished and the cypress shade is the reason to go in July. Paddlers work the backwaters where the current is nothing.

name: Gallery Theatre
unique: A community theater in a small river town running plays, musicals and dinner shows with local casts, in a county where the nearest professional stage is an hour away.
buzz: The productions are ambitious and the audiences are loyal. People drive from other counties for the bigger musicals.

name: Historic Hope
customer: History travellers, architecture fans, school groups
unique: The 1803 house of Governor David Stone on the edge of a pocosin, with original outbuildings, a detached kitchen, formal gardens and a museum that covers both the governor's career and the enslaved people who worked the plantation.
buzz: The house and the grounds are beautifully kept and the interpretation does not skip the slavery. People pair it with the Windsor town walk.

name: Windsor and the Cashie River
unique: A town on a bluff above the Cashie with a grid of nineteenth century houses, a waterfront park and a paddle trail that runs from Windsor down the Cashie through cypress swamp toward the Albemarle.
buzz: The paddle trail is the draw for people with boats and the town walk fills the rest of the day. It is quiet and the river is the color of tea.

name: Bertie County Peanut and Cotton Country Drive
unique: Back roads through peanut, cotton and soybean fields and old plantation land along the Roanoke and Cashie, past country stores, churches and farm stands in one of the most productive agricultural counties in the state.
buzz: The scale of the fields and the emptiness of the roads are the experience. People stop at the country stores for boiled peanuts and lunch.

name: Historic Jackson
unique: A village built around an 1858 courthouse with a pyramid roof, with a self guided walking tour past churches, storefronts and houses that have changed very little since the railroad and cotton years.
buzz: The courthouse is one of the most photographed in the state and the town has kept its grid intact. People describe it as a place where the walking tour takes an hour and the town is happy to see you.

name: Roanoke Rapids Lake
dates: Year round, best spring to fall
unique: Forty six hundred acres of water on the Roanoke with fifty miles of shoreline, a fishing pier and kayak access on the north bank, and campsites where the lake narrows toward the dam.
buzz: Anglers fish it for largemouth and stripers and the lake is quiet compared to Gaston upstream. Birders work the coves in winter for loons and eagles.
